t: You're on Shaftesbury Avenue, a major road in the West End. It runs north-east from Piccadilly Circus to New Oxford Street, crossing Charing Cross Road at Cambridge Circus. The first stretch is in the City of Westminster, and the rest is in Camden. It's named after the 7th Earl of Shaftesbury, a Tory politician and philanthropist. Known as the Poor Man's Earl, he campaigned for better working conditions, reform of the lunacy laws, education, and limits on child labour. He was also a leading figure in the evangelical movement in the Church of England.
